picks.title: LLMs Are Still Making Election Deepfakes Just Days Before the US Midterms
picks.excerpt: The Brennan Center tested AI chatbots to see if they would generate images with false election claims. The results were unsettling, writes Abdiaziz Ahmed.
picks.rationale: New test results from the Brennan Center: mainstream chatbots still produced false election imagery days before the US midterms. AI is the whole story. The copy should attribute the findings and the method to the Brennan Center, name no party, and describe what the models did rather than judge them.

picks.title: EXCLUSIVE: China offered European Commission to join its AI alliance
picks.excerpt: China invited the European Commission to join its AI alliance; the EU executive is already part of a rival US-led initiative to secure AI development.
picks.rationale: A concrete diplomatic move in AI geopolitics: Beijing formally invited the Commission into its AI alliance, which already sits in a rival US-led bloc. This is an exclusive based on reporting, so the copy should attribute it to Euractiv and say the Commission has not answered unless the article says it has.

picks.title: Washington Senate Democrats allege GOP-backed PAC broke AI ad law
picks.excerpt: Washington Senate Democrats allege a GOP-backed PAC's mailer used AI-generated content in violation of the state's election law on synthetic media in campaign ads.
picks.rationale: A new complaint and an early enforcement test of a state law on disclosing synthetic media in campaign ads. NEUTRALITY: the AI-content claim is an allegation from one caucus. The copy must attribute it ('allege'), include the PAC's response if Axios reports one, and focus on what the law requires.

picks.title: EU member states finalize Digital Omnibus negotiating stance
picks.excerpt: The Council of the European Union announced an agreement on its negotiating position on the proposed Digital Omnibus aimed at amending and simplifying the EU's digital rulebook, including the EU General Data Protection Regulation, the ePrivacy Directive and more.
picks.rationale: An official Council decision: member states agreed their Digital Omnibus position, which covers the legal basis for training AI under the GDPR. It is a negotiating stance ahead of trilogues, not adopted law. The copy should say so and lead with the AI-training provisions so the story passes the delete-AI test.

picks.title: Meta delays new business terms after publisher pushback on AI scraping
picks.excerpt: Legal experts argued that Meta's changes weren't enough to rule out AI scraping.
picks.rationale: FOLLOW-UP to the 10-22 card on publishers pressing Brussels and London. The new event is Meta's decision to postpone its AI-scraping business terms to Nov 20. Lead with the delay, not the earlier complaints, and attribute the claim that the changes are 'not enough' to the legal experts quoted.

https://www.theverge.com/tech/1017450/me.new_action: Meta decided to delay its new business terms (the ones publishers say allow AI scraping) to Nov 20 after the publisher pushback. This is a new corporate decision that comes after the 10-22 complaint card.
